h1: Thorough Eye Exams for Seniors in Pine Beach
lede: Reading glasses that never seem strong enough, more glare at night, colors that look a little faded—some changes come with age, and some deserve a closer look. At Academy Vision, we make time to check both your vision and the health of your eyes, and Medicare is one of the plans we accept. You’ll find us on Route 9 near the Mizzen Avenue light in Pine Beach, in a standalone building with its own parking lot and a ramp for patients who need it.

sections.heading: Many Age-Related Conditions Start Quietly
sections.html:
Several eye conditions that become more common later in life develop slowly and without pain. Glaucoma can narrow side vision so gradually that it’s hard to notice. Macular degeneration affects the sharp, central vision you use to read, drive and recognize faces. Cataracts cloud the eye’s natural lens over time, and diabetes can affect the retina’s tiny blood vessels before your sight changes at all.

That’s why a regular exam matters even when you feel fine. Catching a change early gives you and your eye doctor more time to act.

sections.heading: Time, Follow-Through and Straight Answers
sections.html:
• Time. Our optometrists take the time to listen and explain, so your visit doesn’t feel hurried.
  • Ongoing monitoring. We monitor your eye health closely and help catch potential issues early, comparing each visit with the last.
  • Plain explanations. We talk through anything we find in plain language you can understand.

sections.heading: What Your Exam Looks At
sections.html:
1. Your concerns and health history. Share what’s changed, and bring a list of your medications, since some can affect the eyes.
  2. Your prescription. We check your prescription to make sure you’re seeing clearly, whether that’s for reading, hobbies or the drive home.
  3. Eye teamwork. We evaluate how your eyes are working as a team.
  4. Your eye health. We take a close look for signs of conditions such as glaucoma, macular degeneration and cataracts.
  5. What comes next. If something needs attention, we explain your options and keep a close watch over time.

sections.heading: A Practice Families Have Known for Decades
sections.html:
Academy Vision has been caring for local families since 1984, and for over 40 years, families in and around Pine Beach have trusted us with their vision. It’s not unusual for us to see grandparents, parents and kids from the same family, all in the same week.

Our optometrists include Dr. Tyler Lesko, whose clinical focus includes early detection and monitoring of glaucoma, macular degeneration and cataracts, and Dr. Marc Ullman, who manages chronic ocular disease.

sections.heading: Why Tracking Over Time Matters
sections.html: A one-time vision check shows how your eyes look on a single day. Many age-related changes are slow, so much of the value comes from comparing one exam with the next. Returning to the same practice means your optometrist can see what’s different since your last visit and talk with you about it sooner.

sections.heading: When You Need More Than a Routine Visit
sections.html: If your exam shows signs of a condition, our medical eye care includes ongoing management of conditions such as glaucoma and macular degeneration. For cataracts, we monitor how they progress and, when the time is right, coordinate with New Jersey eye surgeons so you receive care before and after surgery.

faq.a: Medicare is one of the plans we accept, and you’ll find the others on our insurance page. What’s covered depends on your plan and the purpose of your visit. Medical insurance comes into play when there’s a health-related concern with your eyes, and our team will help you sort out your benefits and explain what’s covered.

faq.q: How often should I have my eyes checked?
faq.a: There’s no single schedule that suits everyone. Many older adults are advised to have an eye exam every year, and people managing glaucoma, diabetes or macular degeneration may need to come in more often. Ask your optometrist what makes sense for you.

faq.q: What if my vision changes suddenly?
faq.a: Don’t wait for your next appointment. Sudden vision loss, a curtain or shadow over your vision, or flashes of light with a sudden shower of new floaters are reasons to seek emergency care immediately. For other changes that worry you, call us at (732) 978-9306.

cta.heading: Schedule a Senior Eye Exam in Pine Beach
cta.html: Call us at (732) 978-9306 or book online. If you have questions about Medicare or another plan, our team can go over your benefits with you so you know what to expect.
